cards.headline: Dwyer 2013: phosphorus fell dose-dependently on ferric citrate over 28 days (−0.1, −1.9 and −2.1 mg/dL at 1, 6 and 8 g/day); stool discoloration the most common adverse event
cards.summary: Dwyer 2013: phosphorus fell dose-dependently on ferric citrate over 28 days (−0.1, −1.9 and −2.1 mg/dL at 1, 6 and 8 g/day); stool discoloration the most common adverse event
cards.type: Phase 3 multicentre open-label randomised dose-response trial (up to 28 days)
cards.people: 151 participants on maintenance haemodialysis randomised to ferric citrate 1, 6 or 8 g/day.
cards.result: Phosphorus change was dose-dependent: −0.1 ± 1.3 mg/dL (1 g/day), −1.9 ± 1.7 mg/dL (6 g/day) and −2.1 ± 2.0 mg/dL (8 g/day). The most common adverse event was stool discoloration.
cards.watchOut: Open-label and only 28 days — a dose-finding limb, supporting the phase 3 result rather than standing alone.
cards.source: Dwyer JP et al. Dose-response and efficacy of ferric citrate to treat hyperphosphatemia in hemodialysis patients: a short-term randomized trial. Am J Kidney Dis. 2013. PMID: 23369827. cards.headline: Yokoyama 2014: JTT-751 (ferric citrate) was non-inferior to sevelamer for phosphate lowering over 12 weeks (−0.82 vs −0.78 mmol/L; difference −0.03 mmol/L, 95% CI −0.13 to 0.07)
cards.summary: Yokoyama 2014: JTT-751 (ferric citrate) was non-inferior to sevelamer for phosphate lowering over 12 weeks (−0.82 vs −0.78 mmol/L; difference −0.03 mmol/L, 95% CI −0.13 to 0.07)
cards.type: Phase 3 multicentre randomised open-label head-to-head trial (12 weeks)
cards.people: 230 haemodialysis patients randomised to JTT-751 (ferric citrate) 1.5–6.0 g/day or sevelamer hydrochloride 3.0–9.0 g/day.
cards.result: Phosphate change was −0.82 mmol/L (≈ −2.5 mg/dL) on JTT-751 vs −0.78 mmol/L (≈ −2.4 mg/dL) on sevelamer, establishing non-inferiority (least-squares mean difference −0.03 mmol/L, 95% CI −0.13 to 0.07). Diarrhoea was more frequent with JTT-751 and constipation with sevelamer; ferritin and transferrin saturation rose significantly on JTT-751.
cards.watchOut: Non-inferiority against an active comparator, open-label — 'non-inferior to sevelamer' must not be printed as a placebo-controlled effect.
cards.source: Yokoyama K et al. A randomized trial of JTT-751 versus sevelamer hydrochloride in patients on hemodialysis. Nephrol Dial Transplant. 2014. PMID: 24376274. shelves.title: Polystyrene-sulfonate binders (sodium/calcium polystyrene sulfonate) for hyperkalaemia in CKD
shelves.question: In adults with chronic kidney disease (non-dialysis or on haemodialysis) and hyperkalaemia, do the polystyrene-sulfonate binders (sodium polystyrene sulfonate, SPS; calcium polystyrene sulfonate, CPS), compared with placebo, no binder or a newer binder, lower serum potassium?

shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (lowers serum potassium) — the composition leads: the only placebo-controlled report in this base enrols 33 outpatients for 7 days in mild hyperkalaemia (between-group difference −1.04 mEq/L). The CPS dose trial (107 patients) has NO placebo or untreated arm; the CPS crossover (58 patients) compares against blank control; and the largest report (120 patients) is a head-to-head the old binder lost on speed (normokalaemia at 6 weeks on SPS vs 2 weeks on sodium zirconium cyclosilicate). Nothing here addresses acute severe hyperkalaemia, hard outcomes, or the historical intestinal-necrosis safety question — no report is powered for it. Dose misprint flagged: the CPS dose trial's abstract prints its doses as 15 or 30 mg/day in its methods line but 15 or 30 g/day in its conclusion; this pack prints g/day, the trial's actual doses. The newer binders' own questions stay homed at live #301 and live #1059 — cross-point only.

cards.headline: Lepage 2015: SPS beat placebo over 7 days in mild hyperkalaemia (between-group potassium difference −1.04 mEq/L, 95% CI −1.37 to −0.71) — the base's only placebo-controlled trial
cards.summary: Lepage 2015: SPS beat placebo over 7 days in mild hyperkalaemia (between-group potassium difference −1.04 mEq/L, 95% CI −1.37 to −0.71) — the base's only placebo-controlled trial
cards.people: 33 outpatients with CKD and mild hyperkalaemia (potassium 5.0–5.9 mEq/L), randomised to SPS 30 g orally once daily or placebo.
cards.result: SPS was superior to placebo (mean between-group potassium difference −1.04 mEq/L, 95% CI −1.37 to −0.71). Normokalaemia was attained by 73% vs 38% (P = 0.07, not significant). There was a trend toward more electrolyte disturbances and gastrointestinal side effects on SPS.
cards.watchOut: Thirty-three patients, 7 days, mild hyperkalaemia only. This single small trial carries the entire placebo contrast for a drug class used for decades — it must not be inflated into proof for severe or acute hyperkalaemia.

cards.headline: Wang 2023: CPS lowered potassium dose-dependently over 1 week (−0.64 ± 0.37 mmol/L at 15 g/day; −0.94 ± 0.49 mmol/L at 30 g/day) — no placebo group; abstract dose misprint flagged
cards.summary: Wang 2023: CPS lowered potassium dose-dependently over 1 week (−0.64 ± 0.37 mmol/L at 15 g/day; −0.94 ± 0.49 mmol/L at 30 g/day) — no placebo group; abstract dose misprint flagged
cards.type: Prospective open randomised single-centre dose trial (1 week, no placebo or untreated arm)
cards.people: 107 patients with stage 3–5 non-dialysis CKD and hyperkalaemia, randomised to CPS 15 or 30 g/day.
cards.result: Potassium fell by 0.64 ± 0.37 mmol/L (15 g/day) and 0.94 ± 0.49 mmol/L (30 g/day) at day 7, with no significant change in sodium, phosphorus or calcium. Constipation was the most common adverse reaction; no treatment-related serious adverse events were observed.
cards.watchOut: ABSTRACT MISPRINT (flagged, not propagated): the abstract's methods line prints the doses as 15 or 30 mg/day while its conclusion and the trial design give 15 or 30 g/day — a thousand-fold internal inconsistency. This card prints g/day. With no control arm, the falls are within-group changes, not controlled effects.

cards.headline: Wang 2018: on CPS, 61% of haemodialysis patients were below the 5.5 mmol/L potassium safety level vs 32% on blank control (P < 0.01)
cards.summary: Wang 2018: on CPS, 61% of haemodialysis patients were below the 5.5 mmol/L potassium safety level vs 32% on blank control (P < 0.01)
cards.type: Prospective randomised crossover trial (CPS 15 g/day for 3 weeks vs blank control, 1-week washout)
cards.people: 58 maintenance haemodialysis patients with interdialytic hyperkalaemia.
cards.result: Potassium below the 5.5 mmol/L safety level in 61% on CPS vs 32% on control (P < 0.01); peaked T-waves were less frequent on CPS (13.8% vs 31.0%, P < 0.01). CPS also reduced phosphorus, with no effect on calcium, sodium, volume or blood pressure.
cards.watchOut: The comparator is blank control (no placebo) in a crossover — a real but weaker contrast than a parallel placebo-controlled trial.

cards.headline: Elsayed 2025: SPS lowered potassium but reached normokalaemia more slowly than sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (6 weeks vs 2 weeks, P < 0.001 between groups)
cards.summary: Elsayed 2025: SPS lowered potassium but reached normokalaemia more slowly than sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (6 weeks vs 2 weeks, P < 0.001 between groups)
cards.type: Prospective double-blind randomised multicentre head-to-head binder trial (8 weeks)
cards.people: 120 haemodialysis patients with predialysis potassium >5 mmol/L, randomised to sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (SZC) 5 g thrice weekly or SPS 15 g thrice weekly on non-dialysis days.
cards.result: Potassium fell significantly in both groups from week 1; the SZC group reached normokalaemia after 2 weeks vs 6 weeks on SPS (P < 0.001 between groups). Rescue therapy was needed by 3.3% (SZC) vs 6.6% (SPS) (p = 0.678). Gastrointestinal side effects were 5% vs 11.6%, and SPS was significantly less palatable (p < 0.001).
cards.watchOut: A head-to-head the old binder lost on speed — printed as such. SZC's own question stays homed at live #1059 / live #301; this card reports the SPS arm's performance only.
cards.source: Elsayed MM et al. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate versus sodium polystyrene sulfonate for treatment of hyperkalemia in hemodialysis patients: a randomized clinical trial. BMC Nephrol. 2025. PMID: 40329202. Registry ID: NCT06029179. cards.summary: Synthesis: the original potassium binders lower potassium — POSSIBLE, resting on one small placebo-controlled trial
cards.people: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional population.
cards.result: Four reports: one 33-patient, 7-day placebo-controlled SPS trial (−1.04 mEq/L); an uncontrolled CPS dose trial (dose-dependent falls; abstract mg/g dose misprint flagged and not propagated); a CPS crossover vs blank control; and a head-to-head in which SPS was slower than SZC. cards.watchOut: Never let the 7-day, 33-patient result stand in for seven decades of assumed efficacy, and never print the CPS dose trial's methods-line mg/day doses — the doses are g/day.

shelves.title: Androgens (nandrolone decanoate above all) for anaemia in patients on dialysis — a four-drug 1981 comparison and null ESA-era adjuvant trials
shelves.question: In patients receiving dialysis with anaemia, do androgens — nandrolone decanoate above all — raise haemoglobin/haematocrit, alone, compared with other androgens, or added to / compared with erythropoietin?

shelves.balance: SPLIT — an era-stratified base whose modern limb is null, and the eras lead. The positive reports are pre-ESA (the 1981 NEJM paper — a FOUR-DRUG sequential comparison of nandrolone decanoate, testosterone enanthate, oxymetholone and fluoxymesterone, labelled as such, never a nandrolone-only trial, with completers falling 77 → 56 → 35 across drug periods) or an EPO-comparator trial in men over 50 on CAPD (2002). Both ESA-era adjuvant trials (1992, n = 12; 2005, n = 32) found NO significant added benefit from nandrolone, and both record tolerability failures (acne withdrawals; four women stopping for hirsutism and hepatic dysfunction). No wording may present this as a live alternative to ESAs. The CAPD trial's nutritional findings are cross-pointed to pack #7836 (nandrolone for lean body mass) and are not counted there.

cards.headline: Neff 1981: injectable androgens (nandrolone, testosterone enanthate) beat oral agents on haematocrit response — a four-drug sequential comparison, not a nandrolone-only trial
cards.summary: Neff 1981: injectable androgens (nandrolone, testosterone enanthate) beat oral agents on haematocrit response — a four-drug sequential comparison, not a nandrolone-only trial
cards.type: Randomised clinical trial comparing four androgens in sequential 6-month drug periods (pre-ESA era)
cards.people: Anaemic patients on maintenance haemodialysis; 77 patients completed the first drug period, 56 the second and 35 the third. Women were not given testosterone enanthate.
cards.result: The injectable androgens (nandrolone decanoate, testosterone enanthate) were clearly superior to the oral agents (oxymetholone, fluoxymesterone) on responder proportion and mean haematocrit rise; approximately half of patients gained at least 5 percentage points of haematocrit on an injectable androgen. Patients who required regular transfusions and those with bilateral nephrectomies did not respond.
cards.watchOut: FOUR-DRUG CLASS COMPARISON with heavy sequential attrition (77 → 56 → 35) — labelled as such on the face, per the binding note. Agent-specific claims for nandrolone alone cannot be read off this design, and the pre-ESA comparator context no longer exists.
cards.source: Neff MS et al. A comparison of androgens for anemia in patients on hemodialysis. N Engl J Med. 1981. PMID: 7010161. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Berns 1992: adding nandrolone to low-dose erythropoietin did not enhance the haematocrit response (0.37 vs 0.32 %/week, not significant) — n = 12
cards.summary: Berns 1992: adding nandrolone to low-dose erythropoietin did not enhance the haematocrit response (0.37 vs 0.32 %/week, not significant) — n = 12
cards.type: Prospective randomised adjuvant trial (up to 16 weeks)
cards.people: 12 chronic haemodialysis patients (6 + 6): low-dose recombinant erythropoietin 40 U/kg intravenously thrice weekly alone vs with nandrolone decanoate 2 mg/kg intramuscularly weekly.
cards.result: The weekly haematocrit rise was 0.37 ± 0.11%/week with the combination vs 0.32 ± 0.13%/week on EPO alone (not significant). The 30% haematocrit target was reached by 1 of 6 on the combination vs 3 of 6 on EPO alone. Two combination patients asked for nandrolone to be stopped for unacceptable side effects (acne).
cards.watchOut: A 12-patient trial — far too small to exclude a modest effect, but its point estimate and target attainment both favour EPO alone, and it is one of two null ESA-era adjuvant trials.
cards.source: Berns JS et al. A controlled trial of recombinant human erythropoietin and nandrolone decanoate in the treatment of anemia in patients on chronic hemodialysis. Clin Nephrol. 1992. cards.headline: Navarro 2002: nandrolone raised haemoglobin as much as erythropoietin in men over 50 on CAPD (8.9 → 11.8 g/dL vs 8.5 → 11.7 g/dL over 6 months)
cards.summary: Navarro 2002: nandrolone raised haemoglobin as much as erythropoietin in men over 50 on CAPD (8.9 → 11.8 g/dL vs 8.5 → 11.7 g/dL over 6 months)
cards.people: 27 stable men over 50 on continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis: recombinant erythropoietin (n = 14) vs nandrolone decanoate 200 mg/week intramuscularly (n = 13).
cards.result: Haemoglobin rose similarly in both groups (8.5 ± 0.9 → 11.7 ± 0.6 g/dL on EPO; 8.9 ± 0.8 → 11.8 ± 0.4 g/dL on nandrolone; haematocrit 25.8% → 34.7% vs 27.0% → 35.1%). The nandrolone group's nutritional indices also improved — cross-pointed to pack #7836, not counted there.
cards.watchOut: Men over 50 on CAPD only, 27 patients, against EPO as comparator (not placebo): it shows nandrolone can raise haemoglobin, in an era and population where EPO was the alternative — not that it adds anything to EPO.
cards.source: Navarro JF et al. Randomized prospective comparison between erythropoietin and androgens in CAPD patients. Kidney Int. 2002. PMID: 11918762. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Sheashaa 2005: adding nandrolone to low-dose EPO raised haemoglobin in both groups with no significant between-group difference; four women stopped nandrolone for adverse effects
cards.summary: Sheashaa 2005: adding nandrolone to low-dose EPO raised haemoglobin in both groups with no significant between-group difference; four women stopped nandrolone for adverse effects
cards.people: 32 anaemic adult haemodialysis patients with adequate iron stores: low-dose EPO 1,000 U thrice weekly with vs without nandrolone decanoate 50 mg intramuscularly twice weekly.
cards.result: Haemoglobin and haematocrit rose significantly in both groups (p < 0.001) but the between-group difference was not significant. Four female patients discontinued nandrolone for adverse effects, principally distressing hirsutism and hepatic dysfunction.
cards.watchOut: The second null ESA-era adjuvant trial, with the base's clearest harm signal — androgen harms in women are part of this shelf's balance, not a footnote.

cards.headline: Synthesis: androgens raised haemoglobin before ESAs existed; as EPO adjuvants they added nothing — SPLIT by era
cards.summary: Synthesis: androgens raised haemoglobin before ESAs existed; as EPO adjuvants they added nothing — SPLIT by era
cards.people: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional population.
cards.result: The 1981 four-drug comparison (injectables superior to orals) and the 2002 CAPD head-to-head (nandrolone ≈ EPO) are positive; both ESA-era adjuvant trials (n = 12 and n = 32) are null, with acne withdrawals and four women stopping for hirsutism and hepatic dysfunction. The founding evidence for a drug still encountered in dialysis practice is era-bound and is presented as history, not as an ESA alternative.
cards.watchOut: Never cite the 1981 paper as a nandrolone-only trial, and never pool the pre-ESA positives with the ESA-era nulls into a single average claim.

shelves.title: Nandrolone decanoate for lean body mass and muscle function in kidney failure (dialysis and predialysis)
shelves.question: In patients with kidney failure (on dialysis, or predialysis with malnutrition), does nandrolone decanoate, compared with placebo or conventional treatment (alone or factorially with resistance exercise), increase lean body mass and muscle function?

shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit on lean body mass, a surrogate) — a lean-mass surrogate base with one discordant nutritional signal, and the split leads. All three reports are small (29–79 patients, 12 weeks to 6 months) and their shared positive outcome is lean body mass; no report measures falls, hospitalisation or survival. The two dialysis reports are positive (+4.5 vs +1.9 kg vs placebo; +3.1 kg in the factorial trial, where exercise did not significantly increase lean mass). The one predialysis report (malnourished patients, GFR 5–30 mL/min — population labelled, not silently pooled with the dialysis reports) also raised lean mass BUT serum albumin FELL (P < 0.05) — printed on the face beside the dialysis positives, per the binding note. Androgen harms from the sister shelf #7835 (hirsutism, hepatic dysfunction, acne withdrawals) belong on this face too, cross-pointed. The CAPD trial carded at #7835 reported nutritional secondaries and is cross-pointed only, never counted twice (one-home rule).

cards.headline: Johansen 1999: nandrolone increased lean body mass more than placebo over 6 months (+4.5 ± 2.3 kg vs +1.9 ± 1.6 kg, P = 0.005 between groups)
cards.summary: Johansen 1999: nandrolone increased lean body mass more than placebo over 6 months (+4.5 ± 2.3 kg vs +1.9 ± 1.6 kg, P = 0.005 between groups)
cards.people: 29 patients on dialysis for at least 3 months: nandrolone decanoate 100 mg intramuscularly weekly (n = 14) vs placebo (n = 15).
cards.result: Lean body mass rose +4.5 ± 2.3 kg on nandrolone vs +1.9 ± 1.6 kg on placebo (P = 0.005 between groups). Serum creatinine rose on nandrolone (+168 µmol/L (1.9 mg/dL)) but not placebo, consistent with increased muscle mass. Walking and stair-climbing time improved on nandrolone (36.5 → 32.7 s).
cards.watchOut: Twenty-nine patients and a surrogate outcome (lean mass by absorptiometry); the creatinine rise is a muscle-mass marker here, not a kidney-function change. Grip strength did not change in either group.
cards.source: Johansen KL et al. Anabolic effects of nandrolone decanoate in patients receiving dialysis: a randomized controlled trial. JAMA. 1999. PMID: 10208142. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Johansen 2006: nandrolone increased lean body mass by +3.1 ± 2.2 kg (P < 0.0001); resistance exercise did not significantly increase lean mass but increased quadriceps area and strength
cards.summary: Johansen 2006: nandrolone increased lean body mass by +3.1 ± 2.2 kg (P < 0.0001); resistance exercise did not significantly increase lean mass but increased quadriceps area and strength
cards.type: Randomised 2×2 factorial trial (12 weeks): nandrolone or placebo × intradialytic lower-extremity resistance exercise
cards.people: 79 maintenance haemodialysis patients randomised (68 completed); weekly nandrolone decanoate (100 mg women; 200 mg men) or placebo injections, with or without resistance exercise.
cards.result: Nandrolone increased lean body mass by +3.1 ± 2.2 kg (P < 0.0001). Exercise did not significantly increase lean body mass, but quadriceps cross-sectional area rose with both interventions additively; exercise increased strength in a training-specific fashion and improved self-reported physical functioning (P = 0.04).
cards.watchOut: A factorial design: the nandrolone and exercise effects must not be merged. Twelve weeks is short for a body-composition claim.
cards.source: Johansen KL et al. Effects of resistance exercise training and nandrolone decanoate on body composition and muscle function among patients who receive hemodialysis: A randomized, controlled trial. J Am Soc Nephrol. 2006. PMID: 16825332. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.summary: Johansen 2006 (labelled exercise-limb slice of the same factorial trial, never a second report): exercise improved strength and self-reported functioning without significantly increasing lean mass
cards.type: Labelled slice — the exercise limb of the 2×2 factorial trial carded above
cards.people: The same 79-patient factorial trial carded above; this slice reports its exercise limb only.
cards.result: Exercise did not significantly increase lean body mass; quadriceps cross-sectional area increased with exercise (additively with nandrolone), strength increased in a training-specific fashion, and self-reported physical functioning improved (P = 0.04).

cards.headline: Eiam-Ong 2007: in predialysis CKD with malnutrition, nandrolone increased lean body mass (P < 0.01) BUT serum albumin fell (P < 0.05)
cards.summary: Eiam-Ong 2007: in predialysis CKD with malnutrition, nandrolone increased lean body mass (P < 0.01) BUT serum albumin fell (P < 0.05)
cards.type: Randomised trial vs conventional treatment alone (3 months) — PREDIALYSIS population, labelled
cards.people: 29 predialysis CKD patients (GFR 5–30 mL/min) with moderate-to-severe malnutrition: nandrolone decanoate 100 mg intramuscularly (n = 16) plus conventional treatment vs conventional treatment alone (n = 13).
cards.result: Lean body mass increased on nandrolone (P < 0.01 within group; change significantly greater than control, P < 0.05) but serum albumin fell (P < 0.05). There was no change in protein catabolic rate, lipids, haematocrit or GFR. Minor adverse effects occurred in a few nandrolone patients.
cards.watchOut: The albumin fall is printed on the face per the binding note: lean mass rose while the standard nutritional marker fell — the two must never be separated. This is a predialysis, malnourished population, not a dialysis population.
cards.source: Eiam-Ong S et al. Nutritional effect of nandrolone decanoate in predialysis patients with chronic kidney disease. J Ren Nutr. 2007. PMID: 17462549. Registry ID: none in the record.
